Instead, the evidence discusses 'normal deviation' (η̄) as a component in a complexity score used to allocate resolution levels. It states that artifact ratios (including topological ones) decrease as resolution increases, implying that insufficient sampling (due to coarse resolution in complex regions) leads to artifacts, rather than errors in estimating the normal direction itself. The text treats the normal as a given input for the pivot representation, not as an estimated value subject to error that causes topology issues.
